Question: Of all the causes of WWI, what was most responsible/impactful?

Militarism, Alliance System, Nationalism, Transformation (social, cultural, economic, intellectual), Imperialism, Shooting. (MANTIS)

Groups will be doing a google slide deck, presenting their topic as the dominant cause. The presentations should be around 6 slides long and presented as a visual essay. The first slide should contain 3 sentences of relevant context. The second slide is their thesis, making the case for their topic as the central cause. The next slides (2-3) should include the central evidence for their argument, including historical examples and dates. The 5th slide should present a counterargument (one of the other MANTIS causes) and refute or qualify. The final slide should be the conclusion, including a synthesis (expansion of the argument) point. They should include images, including maps, if applicable. Groups will present them on Thursday.

This will be a graded presentation in the classwork category (same as Socratic Seminars). All members of the group should participate and should avoid reading extensively from the slides.

Author: Who authored the piece? What is the author’s point of view, how might this impact the document? Consider: gender, age, class, race, nationality, rural/urban, occupation/rank, education, political/ideological affiliation.
Place and Time: When/where was the source produced, and how might this affect the meaning of the document? Are there clues within the document as to the time and place of origin?
Prior Knowledge: What essential background information is needed to understand it?
Audience: Who was the source created for, and how might this affect the reliability of the document? 
Reason: Why was this document produced at the time and place it was? Prior knowledge, time and place, author, audience all factor in to a student being able to determine reason. 
Main Idea: What is the point the document is trying to make? It is essential that students be able to synthesize the information in the source and express it in a single sentence.
Significance: Why is this source important for historians? How does it help understand the time period?
